trafficCapture.title: traffic capture
trafficCapture.desc:
When turned on, all agent''s HTTP traffic will be stored through the historical proxy, and agents will be injected with the traffic_search / traffic_get tools and proxy settings (the prompt will include a proxy description).

When off (default), no traffic is logged. The agent configures proxy settings and traffic tools. without receiving, proxy-related information is also included in the prompt. Not included. When you switch, your agent will be re-created and take effect immediately.

trafficCapture.off: Off · Do not inject records or proxies

agentBinding.title: Agent automatic traffic connection
agentBinding.desc:
The default is off. When enabled, the reporting agent that runs when a vulnerability is logged matches existing HTTP requests/responses, concatenates that traffic, and creates a report. Querying packets and calling additional tools increases token consumption.

It can report normally even if it is TCP, no packets were captured, or there is no matching traffic. This switch does not affect traffic capture, passive connections, or stored evidence viewing. It will be applied starting from the next agent, and if turned off, new automatic connections will be immediately rejected.

When turned on, each task Motion constraints(allow/deny items managed in "Operation Restrictions" in the task overview) are added to the agent''s system prompt to limit the scope of the search (e.g., "Test only the current port" and "No brute force").

plannerand workerYou can control whether or not to inject each, the default is all on. Switching takes effect immediately (you''ll read it next time) and there''s no need to re-create the agent. When turned off, the agent will no longer see constraints.

experimental.desc:
This feature is still being tested and is off by default. It may change agent behavior or affect stability, so understand the impact before turning it on.

noa context compression: Model directly compresses long conversation records (norma v0.4.0). When turned on, there are four types of agents connected to the platform (Planner/Worker/Main Agent/Dialogue) receives the context from noa instead of the built-in compression, and the original compressed text is stored in the working directory of the task, making it easy to review. Switching takes effect immediately (applies to future launches) and does not require you to re-create the agent. Turning it off will immediately restore built-in compression.

connect.title: Retry connection
connect.trigger: If there is no connection or you have not yet received 200: Network layer error such as connection reset / read/write timeout / DNS failure, and HTTP 408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504.
connect.skips: Other status codes (400 / 401 / 403 / 404 / 413 / 422, etc.) are definite rejections, so sending them again will still fail, so raise them immediately.
connect.desc: Send the same request again as is. Once the stream starts (you already get 200), this floor is not responsible if it gets cut off midway.
connect.offHint: -1 = Bump failure immediately up without a single retry.

empty.title: Empty response retry
empty.trigger: HTTP 200 and finish_reason is normal stop, but there is no content block in the entire response. Gateway empty frames, incident field missing frames, and sampling hiccups all appear this way.
empty.skips: Except for cases where there is no content due to being truncated by max_tokens (this must be resolved by increasing the output upper limit, and if you send it again, you will hit the same wall again).
empty.desc: Since the entire prompt is sent again, the cost is high in long contexts, so it is better not to set the number too high.
empty.offHint: -1 = Send an empty response as is.

stream.title: Retry same provider safe section
stream.trigger: Problems that occur after the stream has already been established (received 200): connection is lost midway, provider overloaded, 429 / 5xx error event inside the stream, and no token has been delivered to the caller yet.
stream.skips: Quota exhausted (402 / insufficient_quota, handled by rotation by changing settings), context exceeded (413 / context length, handled by compression), 400 / 401 / 403 / 404 / 422 deterministic rejects are not retried.
stream.desc: Replay the same request again with the same settings. We haven''t passed any output yet, so replaying it won''t duplicate model output or tool execution.
stream.offHint: -1 = When the stream is disconnected, it immediately passes to redoing the intent in the outer layer.

breaker.title: Circular circuit blocking
breaker.trigger: If temporary failures (429, 5xx, network errors) continuously accumulate to the threshold, it is blocked. Deterministic failures such as insufficient balance (402), key expiration (401 / 403), and no model (404) are blocked right from the beginning without looking at the threshold.
breaker.skips: Once successful, it resets to 0, so sometimes troublesome settings don''t slowly build up and get blocked.
breaker.desc: When blocked, it goes on cooldown, and cycling during cooldown will skip this setting. The state is saved in the DB and does not disappear even after restart.
breaker.offHint: -1 = Never block on transient failures (still block on definite failures)

intent.title: redo intent
intent.trigger: If several previous layers fail to block: worker ends with model_error. Either the internal retries have been exhausted, or the stream has already started delivering output and then hangs up (then playback is unsafe and the entire thing has to be rerun).
intent.skips: Quota exhaustion is already handled by rotation by changing the settings, so we will not rerun it here. When a task enters pause/quit/finish, it yields immediately and does not take up backoff time.
intent.desc: Run the entire intent again from the beginning. Since it is the outermost layer, if you rerun it once, the number of times for the inner layers will be multiplied once again.
intent.offHint: -1 = The intent is determined to be blocked immediately without re-executing.

override.label: Retry Override
override.hint: Applies only to this setting and overrides the global default for "Retry and Backoff". If each space is left blank, the global will be followed. Entering -1 in the count turns off retries for this layer. When filling an interval, a fixed interval is used instead of an exponential backoff. Circuit blocking and intent re-execution are per-process and can only be controlled from the global page.

retry.intro: A failed model call goes through five layers of retries, in order from the inside out: <chain>Connection → Empty response → Same provider safe section → Block circular circuit → Re-execute intent</chain>. Since it is your turn to go to the outside only when the inside layer is used up, the number of times <emph>are multiplied together</emph>. If you max out each floor, one shake can burn dozens of requests. Clearing everything is the current default, and is exactly the same as if this page did not exist. The first three layers can be overridden separately in each model settings.

ClosedLoop.title: Closed-loop
ClosedLoop.heading: Improved with attack and defense evidence and verified again with independent data
ClosedLoop.description: Create rule candidates from logs for improvement, and apply the same base rules and candidate rules to attack and normal logs for evaluation that do not overlap. Returns missing, false positive, and missing fields to the priority of next diagnosis and collection verification.
ClosedLoop.invalidId: The connection ID must be a positive integer.
ClosedLoop.requestFailed: Your request could not be processed.
ClosedLoop.tooLarge: Files must be less than 2 MiB. The total of both datasets must also be less than 2 MiB.
ClosedLoop.resultScope: This result is an offline evaluation that applies small rules to logs that the uploader has marked as attack or normal. It does not prove that an actual attack was successful, SIEM alerts were raised, defenses were blocked, or deployments were completed.
ClosedLoop.metricLimits: If the denominator is missing or a required log field is missing, the metric will not be calculated. MTTD is calculated only when both the actual alert time and attack time for each rule are present and there is a provenance check. Results will vary depending on sample size and label accuracy.
ClosedLoop.priorityDescription: Based on the events below, plan to reproduce the attack, check normal traffic, or supplement log collection. It does not perform automatic attack execution or rule deployment.
ClosedLoop.noPriorities: In this data, there are no false positives, false positives, or false positives for the candidate rules. Additional validation with new independent data and real-world detection environments.
ClosedLoop.label: Answer label
ClosedLoop.tuningResults: View data results for improvement · Not a final performance indicator
ClosedLoop.prepareDescription: Prepare two JSONL files with attack and normal answer labels. If the same event ID or identical log contents are included in both datasets, evaluation will be rejected.
ClosedLoop.scenarioPlaceholder: Example: Improved detection of internal file access by anonymous users
ClosedLoop.syntheticScenario: Synthesis example: anonymous internal file access rules
ClosedLoop.syntheticNotice: The current data is a synthetic example for functional illustration. It cannot be used as actual practice, attack, or detection evidence.
ClosedLoop.referenceLimits: Vulnerabilities and incidents are linked selectively. Connection alone does not prove that the logs come from the same attack execution. The original evidence you linked is preserved as a snapshot when saved and can be checked on export.
ClosedLoop.tuningDescription: This is the data used to generate candidates. Put attack and normal events together and give each event a unique ID.
ClosedLoop.evaluationDescription: Data not used to improve candidates. This file will not be sent in the Request for Candidate Proposals. If you change your rules after seeing the evaluation, prepare new independent data.
ClosedLoop.jsonlPlaceholder: One JSON object per row: event_id, label, fields
ClosedLoop.formatDescription: label is attack or benign. In fields, enter the string, number, and Boolean fields of the original log. Labels and IDs cannot be used in detection conditions. Each dataset can have up to 1,000 events, a row of 64 KiB, and two files totaling 2 MiB. Duplicate events with the same fields are rejected even if the label, ID, and time are changed.
ClosedLoop.timestampFormat: The time is optional and is in RFC3339 format. occurred_at is the actual attack observation time, and baseline_alert_at and candidate_alert_at are the alert times generated by each rule in the actual detection environment. Please do not enter offline matching times or estimated times.
ClosedLoop.ruleDescription: If all of the all conditions of any are matched, it is a detection. Only equals (exact match) and contains (contains strings) are supported. It is not a Sigma·Suricata·Splunk rule executor. The input directly references fields inside fields.
ClosedLoop.suggest: Suggest candidates using only logs for improvement
ClosedLoop.suggestDescription: Find the exact field values ​​of attacks missed by the baseline rule and add mismatch conditions to the normal remediation data. Auto-suggestions may overfit, so review them yourself. Fixes to remove existing false positives can be edited by the user.
ClosedLoop.unresolved: Events that have not yet been described as candidates
ClosedLoop.confirmedTimes: Verify that the attack time and alarm time for both rules are actually confirmed in the original log and are linked to the same event.
ClosedLoop.previewStale: The input has changed. Compare again and save.
ClosedLoop.heldOutSameData: This is the result of applying the baseline rule and candidate rule to the same evaluation data.
ClosedLoop.historyDescription: These are the most recent 20 records. Saved data, rules, and results are not modified, and new comparisons are left as separate records.
ClosedLoop.emptyHistory: There are no saved repeats. Prepare your files, compare them and save your first results.
ClosedLoop.immutableSnapshot: These are the rules, labels, rationale and results at the time of saving. This record does not change even if the linked source is modified.
